messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: High error rate detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (5xx spike, 2023r-model). Alert threshold breached: 15m error rate > 8%. See alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/alerts/13245 :rotating_light:
erica: I'm on it. Pulling logs + checking recent deploys. Can someone grab traces and customer list?
mike: I can take traces. Starting tail on inference logs now: `ssh infra@inference-prod-1 'sudo journalctl -u inference -n 500'`
sofia: I have the rollout graph — no deploys in past 3 hours. Routing config unchanged.
erica: Good. Mike, paste any error backtraces you see. Sofia, can you validate if the cold-start cache invalidation job ran?
mike: paste: ```
ERROR RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.2 GiB
  File "/srv/runtime/infer.py", line 482, in handle_request
    output = model.forward(batch)
  File "/srv/runtime/model.py", line 211, in forward
    with torch.no_grad():
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```
sofia: Cache invalidation cron did run at 2024-05-11T02:10:01Z (logs show `kv-cache-prune --age=30d`). There was a concurrent autoscaler activity at ~02:09 that shrank one node pool.
erica: Noted. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler shrank pool under erroneous load estimate, causing OOMs and cascading 5xx. Next steps: - add to timeline - try live mitigation (scale up pool, pin model to q8/kernels) - prepare status page draft.
mike: Scaled the pool back to baseline (3 -> 6 GPUs) via terraform apply (plan ID tf-2024-05-11-732). CPU/memory now stabilizing. Errors dropping: current error rate 6% and trending down.
erica: Timeline entry 1: 2024-05-11T02:05Z alert triggered (5xx spike).
erica: Timeline entry 2: 02:09Z autoscaler reduced node count from 6->3 due to misinterpreted CPU-only metric.
erica: Timeline entry 3: 02:10Z kv-cache prune job ran.
erica: Timeline entry 4: 02:12Z OOMs began on several pods; 02:15Z 5xx rate > 10%.
neil: Drafting status page blurb: "We are investigating increased 5xx errors impacting text generation in us-west-2. Engineers have identified transient GPU OOMs following autoscaler activity and are mitigating by restoring capacity. We will post updates every 30 minutes." Thoughts?
product-ops: Suggest adding impacted customers note: list of customers with >5 errors in last 15m. We should avoid naming customers publicly; mark as 'a subset of customers using high-throughput endpoints'.
erica: Agreed. Also include mitigation steps we took (restored capacity, throttled background prune).
mike: Quick log snippet of affected pod (inference-57): ```
[2024-05-11T02:11:23Z] WARN shard-0: failed to allocate 1.2 GiB for kv cache, OOM
[2024-05-11T02:11:24Z] ERROR shard-0: request_id=ghi789 status=500 model=2023r seq_len=2048 tokens=512
[2024-05-11T02:11:24Z] TRACE shard-0: eviction started for cache_key=abc123
```
sofia: Hypotheses list: 1) Autoscaler mis-calibrated metric (was observing CPU instead of GPU memory). 2) Cache prune + eviction race left higher memory footprint during rebalancing. 3) Model variant runtime kernel selection changed and used more VRAM.
erica: Let's track acceptance criteria for hypotheses. Hypothesis 1 repro test: run autoscaler sim against GPU memory metrics in staging. Hypothesis 2 repro: run prune with controlled load. Hypothesis 3 repro: check model runtime logs for kernel selection changes.
oncall-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff in 45 minutes. New oncall: mike -> sofia. Add handoff note. :bell:
mike: Handoff summary for sofia: - root cause likely autoscaler decision + concurrent cache prune. - mitigation done: restored node pool to 6 GPUs, temporarily disabled automatic prune for us-west-2, added autoscaler alert rule for GPU memory. - open actions: reproduce autoscaler misread in staging, review kernel selection heuristics, draft postmortem timeline. Logs + traces: https://logs.redwood.example/ctx/abc123
sofia: Acknowledged. I'll take the next 2 hours. Handoff note captured.
erica: Customer impact assessment (quick): 
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (text), models: 2023r, 2024-slim (potentially)
- Scope: ~12% of requests to us-west-2 during 02:10-02:25Z returned 5xx
- Customers impacted: small subset of high-throughput customers (~7 customer accounts flagged)
- Severity: P2 (partial outage for subset)

sofia: Working on RCA thread artifact: will collect full pod-level timeline, autoscaler decision logs, and cache job runs. Adding a temporary mitigations checklist to incident doc.
sofia: Mitigations checklist (doing now): - revert autoscaler policy to baseline - add threshold for GPU memory alert - throttle prune job during peak - enable fallback model variant with lower VRAM until we confirm kernel behavior
mike: Metrics: error rate trending to 1.2% after scale up. Latency normalizing. Keeping an eye on queue sizes.
erica: Status page v0.2 (neil take this and iterate): 
DRAFT: "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors impacting text generation requests in our us-west-2 region. Engineers have restored capacity and applied temporary mitigations; we are monitoring system health. Impact: a subset of customers experienced increased failures between 02:10-02:25Z. Next update: in 30 minutes."
neil: Will post in 5. QA me quick pls.
product-ops: Add line: "No customer data was exposed; this is a service availability issue."
erica: Good. sofia, when you get the handoff, confirm root cause steps and final timeline for postmortem. Also tag SRE and Eng-Platform for follow-up.
sofia: Handoff accepted. I'll compile timeline and open a postmortem PR: `github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pulls/2847` with timeline + mitigations + action owners.
erica: Final live note before standdown: system stable at 02:45Z; error rate <1.5% for 15m. We'll keep monitoring and prepare postmortem.
sofia: Postmortem draft items: - immediate cause: autoscaler reduced GPUs due to metric config bug - contributing: concurrent kv-cache prune during rebalance - mitigation: restored pool, disabled prune, new GPU mem alert - actions: add autoscaler unit tests, require GPU metrics in autoscaler policy, schedule prune windowing. Owners: @mike (autoscaler tests), @neil (status + comms), @erica (postmortem lead).
mike: Logged followups in backlog: INF-512 autoscaler tests, INF-513 prune windowing.
erica: Thanks team. Changing channel to #postmortems for write-up phase. Closing incident thread here. :white_check_mark:
